title: Loading the data and reading the question
question: How does the dataset get into the run, and what does the code do with the user's question?
plain_summary: Step 2 reads the file named by --data-file into a pandas table and stores it as user_data.raw_data. If the path is a folder, it also loads a reference graph when the folder holds a .npy file. In the default real-data mode, main then reads the same file a second time with load_real_world_data and replaces raw_data with that copy. If the table has a column literally named domain_index, the code marks the data as mixing several domains, which overrides the LLM's earlier guess. Step 3, process_user_query, makes no model call: the question was already sent to the LLM in step 1, during setup. This function only looks for 'key: value; key: value' text in the query. 'filter: continuous' keeps the numeric columns, and a 'selected_algorithm' key is only printed. Finally main copies the remaining column names into selected_features and visual_selected_features, the feature lists every later step uses.

inputs.what: The query text stored during setup. process_user_query receives it as args.initial_query.

outputs.what: The dataset as a pandas DataFrame, column names taken from the file's header line.
A reference graph from a .npy file when --data-file is a folder; otherwise None.
Set from the data only if a column named domain_index exists: True when it has more than one distinct value.
Set to 'domain_index' when that column exists.
At this point raw_data, or only its numeric columns if the query said 'filter: continuous'. It is replaced in the next step.
The list of column names the statistics step will analyse.
The same list, used for plots and for the pairwise tests.

sequence.what: In offline mode (the default) it reads --data-file with pd.read_csv, or calls load_local_data when the path is a folder. Online mode generates a synthetic dataset instead. It stores the table and any reference graph, then sets the heterogeneity flags when a domain_index column exists.

Only when --data-file is a folder. It looks for config.json, base_data.csv and base_graph.npy. If one is missing, it takes the last .json, .csv or .npy file the folder listing returns. Only a missing CSV is an error.

Runs when --data_mode is real (the default). It reads the file again, as CSV or as a JSON list of records, and prints its shape, first five column names, memory use and column types. main stores the result over the raw_data that load_data just set.

A plain text parser, not an LLM call. If the query contains ';' or ':', it splits it into key: value pairs. 'filter: continuous' keeps only float64 and int64 columns. 'selected_algorithm' is logged but not stored anywhere. With the default query nothing matches, and the table comes back unchanged.
Wires the two steps into state: raw_data comes from load_real_world_data, processed_data from process_user_query. Both feature lists are set to processed_data's column names.

failure_paths.what: When --data-file is a folder and --data_mode is left at real, load_data reads the folder, but this function then gets the folder path and raises ValueError ("Unsupported file format"). A folder works only with --data_mode simulated.

Any path that is not a folder is read with pd.read_csv first. A JSON file therefore reaches load_real_world_data's JSON branch only if that CSV read did not fail. An unknown --simulation_mode or --data_mode raises ValueError.

A ';'-separated part with more than one ':' (for example "ratio: 3:1") makes the unpack on line 135 raise ValueError, which stops the run. Ordinary prose with one colon becomes a key that nothing reads.
'filter: continuous' keeps only float64 and int64 columns, so other numeric types such as int32 or bool are dropped silently.

change_here.what: Read the file once and accept folders in real mode. Today the second read silently wins over load_data's.
The natural place for typed user input (forbidden or required edges, variables to drop, a time index). The CLI currently has no way to pass these, and the 'selected_algorithm' key here has no effect.
The only data-driven heterogeneity check on the CLI depends on the exact column name domain_index. A fork would let the user name the column, or check the column the LLM proposed.

findings.text: The paper says users can impose constraints such as "Variable 'age' cannot be an effect". The CLI's query handling has no field for constraints.
findings.label: code verified

findings.text: On the CLI the time-series flag comes from the LLM's reading of the query in setup. The web demo uses a separate LLM parse of the user message.
findings.label: code verified

findings.text: The file path the user passes is not only a location: it is pasted into the domain-knowledge prompt in the next step. Path and column names are two separate cues to the dataset's identity.
findings.label: code verified

findings.text: The output-folder arguments are parsed but never used, and in real-data mode the file is read twice.
findings.label: partial
